summary: A game loop repeats three steps every frame: update positions, check collisions, and draw. In the browser, requestAnimationFrame() runs the loop once per screen refresh.
notes: requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop) schedules one more frame. gameLoop asks again at the end, so the loop keeps going without blocking the page.

requestAnimationFrame matches the screen's refresh rate, usually 60 times a second but 120 on some screens, so the ball can move faster there. Real games multiply speed by the time since the last frame.
keysDown is a Set of held keys. keydown adds a key and keyup removes it, so holding ArrowLeft moves the paddle smoothly every frame.
pitfall: Using a while (true) loop instead of requestAnimationFrame freezes the tab, because the browser never gets a chance to draw the frame or handle key presses.
shot_note: Mid-game, after holding the Left key.
contrast: JavaScript runs the loop with requestAnimationFrame(), which the browser calls before each screen refresh, where Python uses ontimer() and Java uses a javax.swing.Timer. The canvas has no repaint(), so the loop clears and draws every frame itself.
